messages.author: f4e25631633510c0
messages.subject: WAIC comment page 85 Nimble manual 0.8.0
parts:
Hi all,
I just started to use Nimble (a couple of days ago) and was reading through the manual and trying out some of the elementary features of the package.
First I want to say that I very much like the package. It appears that it extends the capabilities of standard BUGS software considerably.
But I have a problem understanding the meaning and the usefulness of computing WAIC on only the top-level nodes.
To compute WAIC, one needs to compute the full likelihood using all nodes, so what and how can one compute WAIC if the thetas are not monitored. What is computed then?
I tested this on a simple 2-level hierarchical model, first monitoring all stochastic nodes and then i did not explicitly monitor any parameters.
The example consists of cholesterol intakes in 8 centers, with latent means theta_i (i=1, ..., 8) and individual Gaussian data y_ij, with individual SD all equal to sigma.
The theta's have a Gaussian distribution with mean mu and SD = sigma_theta.
So, in the first case I monitored mu, sigma.theta, the theta's, sigma and then I got WAIC=6991, when I did not explicitly monitore any parameter (then Nimble monitors only mu and sigma.theta), then WAIC=7045.
Now I have difficulties to see what expression is used in the second case, and what the usefulness of this calculation.

Any help to get insight is welcome.

Emmanuel Lesaffre

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: WAIC comment page 85 Nimble manual 0.8.0
parts:
hi Emmanuel,

If you do not monitor all stochastic nodes, NIMBLE will simulate them conditional on the  posterior samples for the nodes you do monitor (but not conditional on any child nodes, such as the data). For example if you don't monitor your theta_i latent means, then NIMBLE  will simulate theta_i based on the posterior for the parameters that govern the theta_i values (mu and sigma_theta). In turn the predictive distribution for the observations will be calculated based on the theta_i that have just been simulated rather than the posterior samples of theta_i from the MCMC.

I think Section 2.5 of the Gelman et al. WAIC reference does a nice job of saying why one might want to simulate theta_i rather than conditioning on the posterior samples of theta_i.

Some notes along the lines of what I just said can be found via `help(buildMCMC)`, as can the full citation for the Gelman et al. paper.

-Chris
